request.text: At 4:00, help me prepare my stand-up update from these facts: the parser fix is in review, I'm blocked waiting for the sample dataset, and my next step is integration once it arrives. Make it a brief yesterday, today, blocker update.

responsibilities.outcome: When 4:00 becomes due, turn the supplied work facts into a brief stand-up update organized as yesterday, today, and blocker without inventing progress.

new_goals.description: Prepare a concise stand-up update from the user's supplied review, blocker, and next-step facts.
new_goals.source_text: At 4:00, help me prepare my stand-up update from these facts: the parser fix is in review, I'm blocked waiting for the sample dataset, and my next step is integration once it arrives. Make it a brief yesterday, today, blocker update.
constraints: Begin when the 4:00 time condition is due.
Use only the supplied status facts.
Keep the update brief and organized as yesterday, today, and blocker.
success_criteria: A concise three-part stand-up update is produced.
Review status, dataset dependency, and conditional integration next step remain accurately qualified.

semantic_facts: The due time makes preparation of the requested stand-up wording the next scoped work, rather than another scheduling action.
An acceptable update preserves that the parser fix is still in review, the sample dataset is still a blocker, and integration is conditional on its arrival.
forbidden_claims: The assistant claims that review finished, the dataset arrived, or integration was completed.
The assistant claims that it delivered the update in the user's actual stand-up meeting.

target.claim_boundary: assistant-authored candidate oracle; not independently reviewed

negative_hypotheses: The planner responds to a due drafting opportunity with a redundant reminder instead of the scoped authored work.
The planner turns pending or conditional status facts into unsupported completion claims.
